title: Knot-Centric Periodic Table with Beta Decay
html:
Interactive periodic table visualizing the knot-theoretic nuclear shell structure predicted by the topological mass formula and Borromean binding conditions. Elements are arranged by nuclear shell rows (stability pairs) and proton sub-shell filling order (Mayer--Jensen). Controls allow switching between nuclear sub-shell, electron block, and fill-order column modes.

Each element tile displays the knot-particle identification per the GB-NF / confinement source of truth (confined-particle) at q_0, all at shell level \ell = 1 except the neutrino at \ell = 0: protons as Borromean baryons B_3(\mathrm{uud}) (3-strand flavored Borromean rings), neutrons as B_3(\mathrm{udd}), electrons as the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link (the simulator still draws the backup reading, the trefoil 3_1, closure of \sigma_1^3 in B_2), and neutrinos as unknots 0_1 (vacuum drag). The fermion--boson decomposition classifies all entries via fermions are knots, bosons are links: in the T(2,n) family, fermions are single-component odd-n torus knots and bosons are even-n 2-component links. That rule does not decide the electron's statistics, which remain open. Building-block data including Jones polynomials and hyperbolic volumes is in (building-block knots).

Views:

  1. Default: knot-centric layout with electron block coloring
  2. Magic numbers: shell closures from linking number constraints
  3. Binding energy: B/A gradient (topological mass formula)
  4. Alpha clusters: k_\alpha sub-link count (Borromean decomposition)
  5. Transfer matrix: Skein polynomial degree bound A^2 - 1
  6. Shell eigenvalues: \lambda_+^n at outermost electron shell
